45003.name: Aiken County
45003.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Aiken County EMS is the named transporter. The county says private ambulance and rescue companies help during peak activity without naming them, and Aiken Rescue and Jackson First Alert Rescue Squad also hold 911 transport licences.

45007.name: Anderson County
45007.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Seen on a public page: Medshore Ambulance (Priority Ambulance) with 17 transport units countywide, and Anderson County EMS (15 paramedic quick-response vehicles, non-transport). Not yet confirmed: the role of Fork Rescue Squad and Pelzer Rescue Squad, still licensed for 911 transport after the 2021 consolidation, and whether the Medshore contract (five years from September 2021) was renewed.

45011.name: Barnwell County
45011.note: AmeriPro EMS runs Barnwell County's 911 ambulance service under a county contract that began April 2024.

45013.name: Beaufort County
45013.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Seen on a public page: Beaufort County EMS and Hilton Head Island Fire Rescue. Hardeeville Fire Department launched its own ambulance service on November 28, 2023, and Hardeeville lies partly in Beaufort County; not yet confirmed how that changes county EMS coverage there.

45015.name: Berkeley County
45015.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Goose Creek Fire Department lists its own Medic 1 and Medic 2 units, and Cooper River Partners holds a 911 transport licence. Not yet confirmed from a public source: their role alongside Berkeley County EMS (Hanahan is staffed by the county).

45019.name: Charleston County
45019.note: Municipal fire departments first-respond; county EMS is the transporter.

45021.name: Cherokee County
45021.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Cherokee County EMS is the only 911 transporter licensed in the county, but the county page does not describe ambulance or 911 service. Not yet confirmed from a county statement.

45025.name: Chesterfield County
45025.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Chesterfield County has no county EMS; six volunteer rescue squads (Cheraw, Chesterfield, Jefferson, McBee, Pageland, Patrick) and Lifeguard EMS are licensed. Not yet confirmed: the area each covers.

45027.name: Clarendon County
45027.note: Clarendon County Fire Rescue, the county's combined fire and EMS department, runs the 911 ambulances. East Palmetto Ambulance Service does non-emergency transport only.

45029.name: Colleton County
45029.note: Colleton County Fire & Rescue is the only 911 transporter licensed in the county by the state health department.

45031.name: Darlington County
45031.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Seen on a public page: Darlington County EMS. Hartsville Rescue Squad and Lamar Rescue Squad also hold 911 transport licences; their role is not yet confirmed.

45035.name: Dorchester County
45035.note: County EMS since 1994 (replaced contracted private ambulances).

45037.name: Edgefield County
45037.note: Ambulances are operated by the county.

45039.name: Fairfield County
45039.note: Fairfield County EMS runs the county's 911 ambulances from six stations across the county.

45041.name: Florence County
45041.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Seen on a public page: Florence County EMS. Guardian Ambulance and the Johnsonville, Pamplico and Timmonsville rescue squads also hold 911 transport licences, and Johnsonville's city site says its squad still provides ambulance service; their 911 role is not yet confirmed.

45043.name: Georgetown County
45043.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Three licensed transporters serve the county: Georgetown County Fire/EMS, Midway Fire Rescue and Murrells Inlet-Garden City Fire District. Not yet confirmed from a public source: who answers 911 in which area.
a: Murrells Inlet Rescue dba Murrells Inlet Garden City Fire

45045.name: Greenville County
45045.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Greenville County EMS is the county's 911 ambulance service and also runs the county's EMS dispatch centre (MedCom). Prisma Health Ambulance Service also holds a state ambulance licence in the county; its administrator describes its role as moving patients in and out of Prisma Health facilities, not running a county's 911 operations (The State, April 2026). Prisma Health Ambulance Service also lists 911 response among its services and in June 2025 described reaching heatstroke patients on Jones Gap trails in Greenville County, so whether it answers any 911 calls in the county is not yet confirmed.

45047.name: Greenwood County
45047.note: Greenwood County EMS, a county department, runs the county's 911 ambulances; the county's emergency services director described its crews in May 2025 as the ones who stabilize and transport patients.

45051.name: Horry County
45051.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Seen on a public page: Horry County Fire Rescue and North Myrtle Beach Rescue Squad (volunteer nonprofit). Myrtle Beach Fire Department has its own ambulances; not yet confirmed from a public source that they transport 911 patients, or whether Murrells Inlet-Garden City Fire District covers Garden City Beach in Horry County.

45053.name: Jasper County
45053.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Jasper County Fire-Rescue is seen for the county, but Hardeeville Fire Department has run its own ambulance service since November 28, 2023. Not yet confirmed: the area each covers.

45055.name: Kershaw County
45055.note: Kershaw County EMS (Camden) is the only 911 transporter licensed in the county by the state health department.

45057.name: Lancaster County
45057.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Lancaster County EMS runs paramedic units. Not yet confirmed from a county page that it transports patients and runs the county's 911 ambulances.

45059.name: Laurens County
45059.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Laurens County EMS runs the county's 911 ambulances. The county also contracts with Prisma Health to staff an ambulance with paramedics around the clock (county council, June 2026). Whether the Prisma Health contract ambulance answers 911 calls on its own or staffs a county unit, and in which part of the county, is not yet confirmed.

45061.name: Lee County
45061.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Lee County EMS, a county department, runs four full-time ambulances covering the whole county. A 2024 plan for Lee County Fire Department volunteers to carry patients to hospitals is not yet confirmed as running or as part of the county EMS service.

45063.name: Lexington County
45063.note: Lexington County EMS has 198 staff and up to twenty ambulances. The MedTrust contract runs five years from December 2022, and EMS1 reported it ongoing in June 2025.

45075.name: Orangeburg County
45075.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Seen on a public page: Orangeburg County EMS. A supplemental MedTrust contract began in September 2023 for three years; not yet confirmed from a source after 2023 that it is still in force.

45077.name: Pickens County
45077.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. A 2025 report says the county is adding EMS trucks, with 11 24-hour crews, and a 2012 county page called county EMS the sole 911 provider. Not yet confirmed: the role of Clemson University Fire & EMS (campus 911 calls) and Metrolina Ambulance in Easley.

45081.name: Saluda County
45081.note: Saluda County EMS, a county department, runs the county's 911 ambulances from its Saluda headquarters and substations.

45083.name: Spartanburg County
45083.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Seen on a public page: Spartanburg County EMS, a county department. Not yet confirmed from a public source: the role of Landrum Rescue Squad, licensed for 911 transport, although county EMS has a Landrum station.

45091.name: York County
45091.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Seen on a public page: Piedmont Medical Center EMS (county 911 contractor, including the former River Hills/Lake Wylie service) and Atrium Health Fort Mill EMS. Not yet confirmed from a public source: the role of Tri-Star Medics (Rock Hill, BLS), licensed for 911 transport, and the county franchise ordinance text.
